subject: Post-call recap: Acme Health private VPC / on-prem requirements
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Thompson <alex.thompson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Acme Health private VPC / on-prem requirements

Alex — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so everyone is aligned and we have clear next steps.

Summary of needs / drivers:
- Regulatory & data residency: PHI needs to remain in-region and fenced; Acme requires customer-managed keys and audit logs retained for 7 years.
- Network constraints: All traffic must originate from Acme subnets, and outbound egress to public internet is restricted.
- Air-gap / on-prem option: Due to some facilities, a fully air-gapped deployment (no outbound internet) is a possible later phase.
- Performance targets: sub-200ms 95th p99 for short inference paths; throughput requirement ~40 concurrent sessions initially.

What we proposed on the call:
- Private VPC deployment in your AWS account with Redwood control plane (managed or private control plane option).
- Optional on-prem/appliance package for air-gapped facilities; includes offline model transfer and local KMS.
- Network architecture: transit VPC + VPC endpoints; we recommended a NAT/proxy pattern for optional telemetry with customer approval.

Action items / next steps:
1) Alex / Priya: please share your network ACLs and egress policy doc (we need IP allowlist and port list) — target: by Tue 25 May.
2) Camila/Ben: we'll send a short checklist (network, KMS, audit logs) and a high-level diagram for architecture review — by EOD today.
3) Marissa: pricing ballpark for Dedicated vs Private + on-prem appliance to discuss tradeoffs.
4) Schedule a technical deep-dive with Acme SREs (Priya) next week to walk through firewall/NAT specifics.

Attachments: acmehealth-network-requirements.pdf (stub), redwood-private-deploy-diagram.png (stub).

Thanks — happy to iterate if I missed anything.

—
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Acme Health private VPC / on-prem requirements

Thanks Camila — this looks right. A few clarifications / additions from our side:
- Data residency: production PHI must live in us-east-1 only for now. Staging can be in us-west-2.
- KMS: we will require BYOK via our AWS KMS key; any solution must support CMKs in our account.
- Telemetry: team is comfortable allowing outbound TLS to a restricted set of endpoints if we can put it through a proxy and get an allowlist.
- Air-gap: for facility X we will need a fully offline option; timeline unknown but important for long-term procurement.

I'll work with Procurement and Priya to get the network ACLs and port list to you by Monday EOD.

Also looping in Jordan Lee (Product) who will evaluate product fit — Jordan, Camila/Marissa are our Redwood contacts.

Alex

Alex / team — quick pricing note to set expectations before the deep-dive:
- Private VPC (BYOK, control plane with limited telemetry): estimated list price $12k / month for initial capacity (includes reserved GPU slots and MRC for support).
- Dedicated reserved capacity (Redwood Dedicated) for consistent SLA and higher throughput: $25k / month (1-year commit) — we can show cost tradeoffs vs. per-token hosted later.
- On-prem appliance (air-gap) is a one-time engineering & packaging fee ~ $75k plus a support contract; this is a longer procurement path.

I'll prepare a concise comparison doc and a short TCO table for Wed 26 May.

If it helps, we can run a short POC in your staging region for 2 weeks (low-cost pilot) to validate perf & networking before committing.
